niches.name: Independent Dimensional Metrology and Gauge-Calibration Services for Precision Manufacturers
niches.recommended_action: Review only; initial screen incomplete; no sourcing activation
niches.thesis: Precision manufacturers repeatedly need trusted dimensional measurements and audit-ready gauge records. Independent calibration laboratories can own the recurring equipment-service relationship without manufacturing the instruments or operating customers factories.
niches.growth_tailwind: Verified adjacent-company demand: Transcat FY2025 service revenue grew7%; FY2026 broad service revenue grew20%, including acquisitions. Ongoing precision quality requirements support demand, but exact dimensional-service market CAGR above GDP is unverified.
niches.operational_complexity: More controlled measuring assets create calibration schedules, shipping/return coordination, uncertainty documentation, out-of-tolerance investigations and certificate retention.
niches.second_order_beneficiary: The vendor earns fees maintaining measurement confidence and equipment records across customers production cycles, rather than selling the end products being manufactured.
niches.scope: Dimensional gauges, micrometers/calipers, mechanical measuring tools, periodic calibration/repair and certificate administration. Prefer existing accredited service-heavy labs. Exclude instrument distributors without meaningful service, electrical power testing, medical-physics QA, cosmetic/package product testing, water controls and construction-materials testing.

margins.evidence: Typical EBITDA>=15% unverified. Transcat FY2025 broad service gross margin33.4% is not EBITDA; FY2026 consolidated adjusted EBITDA48.7/331.9=14.7% is mixed-business company data, not niche margin.

recurring_revenue.evidence: Repeated calibration/certification and equipment records supported by provider practices and Transcat. Contracted share, retention and frequency unknown. NIST specifies no universal annual mandate.

industry_growth.evidence: Company growth7% FY2025 /20% FY2026 supports tailwind proxy only; exact niche CAGR unverified.

growth_tam.evidence: Exact US dimensional calibration service TAM unknown; broader calibration figures cannot establish $500M niche floor.

initial_screen.verdict: INCOMPLETE; proceed for human review under headless instruction, not a passed investment screen

niches.name: Robotic-Milking Equipment Preventive Maintenance and Consumable Route Services for Dairy Farms
niches.recommended_action: Review only with travel/OEM/fit flags; initial screen incomplete; no sourcing activation
niches.thesis: Dairy robots require reliable technical support, scheduled maintenance and consumable replenishment throughout their installed life. Regional service providers may earn repeat revenue tied to farm uptime without owning dairy farms or manufacturing robots.
niches.growth_tailwind: USDA2026 publication documents robotic-milking share of US milk rising4% in2016 to6% in2021;13% of150–499-cow farms adopted by2021. This establishes historical adoption tailwind, not current service-market growth.
niches.operational_complexity: Automation replaces some milking labor with robot troubleshooting, hygiene routines, wear-part replacement, diagnostic records and round-the-clock uptime obligations.
niches.second_order_beneficiary: Technicians and consumable routes earn revenue supporting installed robots after farm automation investment; avoid confusing farm ownership, robot manufacturing and service revenue.
niches.scope: Preventive maintenance, emergency repair, wear parts and recurring hygiene-consumable routes for installed robotic milking systems. Existing multi-OEM dealerships may house services; distinguish service earnings from new equipment installation, buildings and real estate.

margins.evidence: Typical service EBITDA>=15% unverified. Anonymous listing implies17.7% across mixed dealer/service business; seller assertion, not industry or standalone service metric.

recurring_revenue.evidence: Consumable routes and installed-base maintenance observable; Mid-Atlantic provider describes monthly-fee service pilot. Contract penetration, retention and mature contract profitability unknown.

industry_growth.evidence: Primary USDA historical automation adoption tailwind supported; exact current service CAGR above GDP not established.

growth_tam.evidence: US robot-maintenance/consumables service TAM unverified; robot hardware or total dairy output cannot substitute.

initial_screen.verdict: INCOMPLETE; full pipeline review with explicit flags, not pass/activation
